item.text: {"question_id":"6B.4","answer":"In 2023, the evidence shows administrative and capacity-building activity, but not enough to establish that Tshisekedi appointed and retained qualified administrators or consistently provided adequate staffing and resources. Presidential appointments and judicial reassignments were documented, including 69 senior magistrates entering office, but the supplied records do not show selection criteria, qualifications, tenure protection, retention, independence, or performance (BATCH-0008-E014; BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0019-E005). UNDP-supported recruitment and training of 2,500 magistrates increased the magistrate ratio from 4.4 to 6.9 per 100,000 people, while 75 judicial police officers were trained and a Criminal Analysis Bureau was established in North Kivu and Tanganyika; however, these measures were materially supported by UNDP and other partners and do not establish nationwide service performance or personal presidential direction (BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0009-E005). The government also reported implementation agencies launching schools, health centres, and other infrastructure under PDL-145T, but the account was executive-reported and concerned ongoing works and projections rather than independently verified completion or quality (BATCH-0023-E001). An ILO-supported workshop trained 11 labour inspectors and produced a plan with performance indicators, while the Inspector General acknowledged major weaknesses that limited the inspection system's ability to perform its legal role; funding and subsequent implementation were not demonstrated (BATCH-0023-E017; BATCH-0023-E018). Broader constraints included insufficient judges, remote courts, and inadequate logistical and financial resources, alongside a health system at breaking point in eastern DRC amid conflict, displacement, outbreaks, and limited water and sanitation; these conditions are adverse but are not personally attributed to Tshisekedi in the supplied evidence (BATCH-0011-E005; BATCH-0003-E013). Procurement evidence is mixed: the World Bank reported strengthened procurement procedures and competitive appointments as part of a government reform program, but with external financing and without establishing execution quality; Reuters reported that the Alfajiri methane tender advanced despite unmet financial criteria and an apparently altered technical report, although the motive and presidential responsibility were not established and officials denied problems (BATCH-0014-E002; BATCH-0009-E007). Later review of 2023 accounts also identified alleged budget overruns, uncertified debts, and works not observed in the field, without identifying the responsible officials or proving personal presidential direction (BATCH-0024-E004). Overall, the record supports some ruler-linked or government-linked institutional activity and limited implementation, but qualified retention, adequate resourcing, transparent procurement, and reliable social-service delivery remain unproven; attribution is especially indirect where donor or agency support predominates.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0023-E017","BATCH-0014-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0023-E018","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0003-E013","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0024-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is concentrated in justice, police, labour inspection, and selected infrastructure rather than the full social-service portfolio.","Appointments and training do not establish qualifications, retention, merit-based selection, adequate staffing, or sustained performance.","Several favorable measures were externally supported or reported by government agencies, limiting isolation of Tshisekedi's personal contribution.","Procurement and budget irregularities are documented as allegations or institutional findings without proof of presidential ordering, benefit, motive, or individual responsibility.","No supplied evidence establishes transparent procurement across social services or independently verified service quality and completion."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization of appointments, recruitment, and training as evidence of qualified professional administration.","Recast PDL-145T implementation agencies and World Bank reforms as limited, qualified evidence rather than proof of professional service delivery or transparent procurement.","Preserved favorable capacity-building evidence while distinguishing government attribution from personal presidential attribution and external partner contribution.","Preserved adverse staffing, resource, procurement, and budget evidence with its stated uncertainty and non-personal attribution limits."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
